description: Data-driven sandbox rules compiled from KB signals, controls, and parameter bindings.

rules.name: New device + low trust + high amount
Multi-engine journey flags without early block
Discrepancy between user goal and agent actions
Agent credentials used from unexpected contexts
Amounts just below thresholds with unnatural consistency
Evolving behavioral patterns in response to detection
Multiple accounts generating similar alert patterns
Transaction patterns that exactly match alert rules
OTP requests without corresponding user action / rapid OTP usage
Login attempts from unusual locations/devices post-contact
Device fingerprint changes between phishing interaction and login
Rapid authentication post-phishing or post-OTP sharing
Caller ID spoofing and scam phone numbers
Biometric match 'too perfect' / Keystroke timing anomalies
Transaction volume has unnaturally constant mean across time windows
Gradual monotonic increase in transaction amounts over time
Low variance in daily/monthly spending patterns
Consistent use of low-risk MCCs for high-risk purchases
Similar threshold-just-below patterns across multiple accounts
High density of transactions near the model's decision boundary
High proportion of approvals near threshold
Sudden increase in approvals for certain feature combinations
Accounts sharing infrastructure (IPs, device fingerprints, email domains)
Accounts with similar temporal lifecycle patterns
Anti-correlated activity timing (one pauses, another starts)
Unusual diversity of behavior across accounts (too heterogeneous)
Suspicious phase-shifted patterns (identical lifecycles, different start dates)
High number of accounts transacting with the same low-risk MCCs in similar amounts
All accounts have similar approval rates or decline patterns
Account creation patterns (batch creation, similar attributes)
Rapid pass-through (arrive and leave within hours)
Funds sent to many unrelated accounts
Sudden change from seasoning to pass-through
Multiple accounts from same underlying fingerprint
Multiple accounts sharing device fingerprint components
Order value vs. payment amount mismatch
Prompt injection patterns in agent inputs
Similar webhook forgery patterns across merchants
High API request rate from single source
Multiple cards from same BIN range
Same device fingerprint across multiple cards
Beneficiary connected to known mule networks
Shared identity attributes across unrelated accounts
Shared device fingerprints across multiple accounts
High clustering coefficient among unrelated accounts
Small, consistent transactions just below thresholds
Shell merchant accounts with no physical presence
Multiple accounts sending to same mule network
High betweenness centrality for key nodes
Identity attributes shared across unrelated accounts
Consent granted for unusually broad scopes
Consent granted for data types inconsistent with user's normal activity
New TPP with unusually high consent conversion rate
TPP requesting scopes inconsistent with declared service
Consent scope disproportionately broad for declared purpose
Unusual API call patterns following consent
API calls to endpoints not needed for declared service
Same TPP with broad consents across multiple customers
TPP API keys used from unusual IP addresses
High volume of data access calls
Amount deviation, urgent payment flags, narrative field anomalies
New or unusual beneficiary BIC/account in high-risk jurisdiction
Unusual message volume from specific participant
Unusual routing paths and multiple intermediary correspondents
Operator credential usage at unusual times or location
Rapid sequence of messages from same operator
Unusual BIC combinations and routing through non-preferred correspondents
Off-hours or holiday submissions and rapid succession of large payments
Unnatural navigation in SWIFT interface and superhuman speed
Beneficiary connections to known mule/crypto networks and rapid onward movement
SWIFT message format anomalies and narrative field unnatural phrasing
Payment to jurisdiction with no prior relationship or unusual corridor
